source.title: SVCCA: Singular Vector Canonical Correlation Analysis for Deep Learning Dynamics and Interpretability
source.authors: M. Raghu; J. Gilmer; J. Yosinski; Jascha Narain Sohl-Dickstein

record.tranche_reason: Compares representations across random initializations and architectures using SVCCA, a different similarity method from the cited neuron-permutation approach.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper's own cross-model representation comparisons. Excluded within-network comparisons across training time, class-logit comparisons, compression results, and cited findings from prior work because they do not measure convergence between independently trained models.
record.test_reason: SVCCA provides an alternative test of shared representations across independently initialized networks. Cross-architecture comparisons also establish incomplete similarity. Appendix B.0.1 supplies a specific argument about dependence on the similarity method.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the cross-model comparisons but is narrower than the authors' overall conclusion. They present SVCCA as a tool for comparing distributed representations, report bottom-up learning dynamics, and motivate freeze training and compression. Their cross-model results show shared directions across seeds and layer-dependent similarity across seeds and architectures.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SVD followed by canonical correlation on activation vectors, rather than the cited prior approach of matching neurons by permutation and correlation.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported similarity varies by layer: initial/final layers are described as similar while middle layers differ; cross-architecture similarity decreases at higher layers.

fits_no_version.finding: Lower convolutional layers of the CIFAR-10 Resnet and Convnet are noticeably similar under DFT CCA.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Different architectures trained on the same task can learn similar lower-layer representation subspaces.

record.problems: The cross-model results are mainly qualitative summaries of figures, with no numerical values or uncertainty estimates stated in the text. Comparisons use the same task/data setting and do not test scale or capability.
record.rows_left_out: None of the cross-model comparison results described in the text were left out. Within-network training-time comparisons and the compression experiments were omitted because they do not measure the claim versions recorded here.

untested.parts: No size or capability sweep testing whether alignment increases.
No paired image-caption or vision-language comparison.
No broad estimate of how many features recur across seeds or identification of their semantic content.
No cross-model representation replacement, stitching, or mapping evaluated for task-performance loss. Projection onto shared directions within a network does not establish interchangeability.
No recurrence of identified interpretable features or circuits across models.
No empirical cross-model comparison across input distributions, neighbourhood settings, or a systematic suite of similarity measures; no demonstrated disappearance of convergence out of distribution.
No plateau over model scale and no causal test of shared training data or objectives versus a common model of reality.

missing.what: Shared-subspace utility and distributedness across seeds: approximately 25 SVCCA directions retain nearly the accuracy of a 512-neuron layer; even 100 selected fc1 neurons cannot maintain the accuracy of 20 SVCCA directions. This directly strengthens V3 beyond the qualitative similarity rows.

Specific methodological argument: plain CCA gives the same correlations when unmatched dimensions are noise or useful distinct information; the SVD step distinguishes these cases. Record this as an analytical example, not an empirical network comparison.

record.verdict_notes: Canonical correlation measures alignment after separate linear transformations; it does not by itself demonstrate functional interchangeability. V7 receives support for incomplete alignment only. Its causal explanation and scale-plateau components remain untested.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size or capability sweep, and no test of alignment increasing with size or performance.
No vision-language or paired image-caption comparisons.
Does not assess individual units or establish which features are shared; the comparisons concern aligned subspaces.
Tests alignment by SVCCA's linear transforms and correlations, not transfer or task-performance loss after mapping representations.
Does not compare interpretable features, neurons, or circuits across models.
Does not compare alternative similarity measures, SVCCA settings, or in-distribution with out-of-distribution inputs for cross-model convergence.
Reports layer-dependent and incomplete similarity, but does not test a plateau over scale or distinguish shared training data/objectives from a common model of reality as its cause.

rows.subject: Two four-hidden-layer fully connected toy regression networks with different random initializations
rows.measure: Visual similarity of top SVCCA-aligned directions
rows.value: The top paired directions are described as almost visually identical up to sign.
rows.note: The paper presents this as a toy demonstration of hidden similarity between representations.
rows.check: Top aligned directions are nearly identical, supporting shared subspaces. Correlation after transforming both representations does not establish interchangeable representations with little task-performance loss, so remove V4.

rows.subject: Two CIFAR-10 convolutional networks with different initializations
rows.operation_detail: Compared layer representations across two initializations using SVCCA.
rows.measure: SVCCA similarity between corresponding layer representations
rows.value: The text describes the initial and final layers as similar.
rows.note: The figure shows a layer-by-layer comparison; the paper's textual summary identifies these layer groups as similar.
rows.check: The caption supports similarity of initial and final layers across seeds. Remove V4: no replacement, stitching, or transfer-performance test is reported.

source_check.locator_found: Appendix E, Figure App.4 introductory paragraph and caption.

rows.subject: Two CIFAR-10 convolutional networks with different initializations
rows.operation_detail: Compared layer representations across two initializations using SVCCA.
rows.measure: SVCCA similarity between corresponding layer representations
rows.value: The text describes middle-layer representations as differing.
rows.note: A qualitative layer-group result; no numerical similarities are stated in the text.
rows.check: Partial describes V3: middle-layer similarity is weaker. The same finding positively supports V7's incomplete-alignment component. Remove V4 because similarity alone does not test interchangeability.

source_check.correct: Use partial for V3 and observed for V7's incomplete-alignment component. The caption reports differing middle-layer representation similarity; it does not test plateauing or causal explanations.
source_check.problem: The shared partial state fits V3 but misstates the direction of evidence for V7, whose incomplete-alignment component is supported.

rows.subject: CIFAR-10 Resnet and Convnet
rows.operation_detail: Compared convolutional-layer representations using DFT-based CCA similarity.
rows.value: The text says the lower layers of the two models are noticeably similar.
rows.note: The figure displays layer-to-layer similarity; the text summarizes the lower-layer pattern.
rows.check: The reported lower-layer similarity is accurate, but it tests neither interchangeability nor increasing alignment with scale. Noticeable similarity alone does not establish V7's incomplete-alignment claim.

rows.subject: CIFAR-10 Resnet and Convnet
rows.operation_detail: Compared convolutional-layer representations using DFT-based CCA similarity.
rows.value: The text says similarity progressively decreases for higher layers.
rows.note: The text also says the Resnet's highest layers are least similar to the Convnet's lower layers.
rows.check: Declining cross-architecture similarity supports the incomplete-alignment component of V7, rather than being a partial occurrence of that claim. Remove V4: no functional interchangeability test is provided.
